# opalstack_app (Resource)

An app of a shell user: a directory, and for most types a process or a PHP pool, that a site routes requests to. Deleting an app deletes its directory, and the API silently drops every site route that pointed at it.

An app made with an `installer_url` whose installer does not succeed ends in the state `INSTALL_FAILED`, which took the API some ten minutes to report when tested. The create then fails and the app stays in state, to be destroyed or replaced. Set `timeouts.create` above the default of ten minutes to see that state reported and not a timeout.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "opalstack_app" "blog" {
  name      = "blog"
  osuser_id = opalstack_osuser.deploy.id
  type      = "APA"

  # Only the keys named here are managed.
  json = jsonencode({ php_version = 83 })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the app, which is also the name of its directory. Changing it replaces the app.
- `osuser_id` (String) UUID of the shell user the app belongs to. An app cannot be moved: changing this replaces it.
- `type` (String) Type of the app: `STA` static, `NPF` Nginx with PHP-FPM, `APA` Apache with PHP-FPM, `CUS` proxied port, `SLS`, `SLP` and `SLN` symbolic links, `SVN` or `DAV`. It changes in place, except to or from `CUS`, which replaces the app: the API assigns a port only when it creates one.

### Optional

- `installer_url` (String) URL of an installer script to run when the app is created. Changing it replaces the app. Leaving it out keeps whatever the app was created with, so an imported app is not replaced.
- `json` (String) Per-type settings as a JSON object, for example `jsonencode({ php_version = 83 })`. Only the keys given here are managed: the API adds settings of its own, and those are left alone and not shown. The `opalstack_app` data source shows all of them.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) UUID of the app.
- `osuser_name` (String) Name of that shell user.
- `port` (Number) Port the API assigned to the app when it was created as a `CUS` app.
- `server_id` (String) UUID of the server the app runs on.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import opalstack_app.blog blog
# or by UUID
terraform import opalstack_app.blog 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
